anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Costing inputs such as row counts, histograms, and correlation statistics are stale, absent, or misleading.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer chooses or reuses a sub-optimal execution plan even though acceptable alternative plans exist.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The engine allocates or retains more memory than the host can safely supply, causing pressure, paging, or OOM events.

When all three root causes manifest concurrently, the workload experiences a multi-layer performance collapse. Poor or missing statistics drive large cardinality errors; the cost model, already skewed, may still pick an ill-suited plan or inappropriately reuse one, amplifying misestimation damage. The selected plans often request exaggerated memory for sorts, hashes, or parallel workers, while the engine’s global memory governance is already over-committed. Observable symptoms therefore include wildly inaccurate estimated vs. actual rows, sudden switches between access paths, exploding join buffers, runaway temp-space and swap usage, erratic query runtimes that worsen with each recompile, frequent plan-cache flushes, and ultimately operating-system level paging storms or database process terminations. Because memory pressure feeds back into the optimizer (e.g., spilling to disk changes cost dynamics) and plan invalidations trigger fresh miscompiled plans, troubleshooting becomes noisy and non-deterministic.

Causal chain: stale or incomplete statistics mislead the cost model, increasing the probability of a poor plan choice. Sub-optimal plans often require more memory—larger hash tables, broader scans, or excessive parallelism—which inflates per-query and global memory footprints. The resulting memory strain provokes paging and forces the engine to evict buffers or flush plan cache entries, causing more recompilations that again consult bad statistics and repeat the cycle. In extreme cases, memory exhaustion triggers OS-level intervention, aborting queries or crashing instances, while the root misestimations and plan churn remain unresolved. This feedback loop between faulty statistics, misguided plan selection, and unchecked memory growth magnifies latency, throughput variability, and stability risks across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: Found partially upgraded DD. Aborting upgrade and deleting all DD tables. Start the upgrade process again.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
